title: Sean McVay, Matthew Stafford, Myles Garrett & Kobie Turner recap the Rams' Week 1 matchup against the 49ers
headline: Rams lost Week 1 to the 49ers in Melbourne; McVay took the blame and gave no personnel news, so the offense's lack of rhythm and Myles Garrett's knee are the things to watch.
summary: McVay opened by calling the loss humbling and said he did not get the team ready. He said the 49ers outplayed the Rams in every phase, including special teams. He said it was a three-point game at halftime. The turning point, in his telling, was a drive that reached the goal line and failed on a QB sneak, after which the 49ers went 99 yards for a touchdown and the game got out of hand. He said the offense never found continuity, never distributed the field, and had communication problems on both sides of the ball. He rejected travel and the no-preseason-games approach as excuses and said the team was rested and ready. He gave no injury updates, no depth chart changes and no usage changes for any player. He said the team has time to clean things up before next Monday night.

injuries.detail: McVay did not address it. Reporters asked Stafford and Garrett about a knee problem, and Garrett said he was focused on staying healthy and was not the player he wanted to be. The severity is unknown.

signals.claim: The passing game should improve once the offense fixes its rhythm and communication issues.
signals.note: The offense struggled to move the ball and finish drives, which lowers confidence in the passing game until it shows improvement.
signals.quote: we were never able to really get any continuity going offensively

signals.note: A knee issue was raised by reporters and addressed only by the players, not McVay. His availability and effectiveness in Week 2 are worth monitoring.

topics.detail: McVay said the game flipped after the offense reached the goal line and failed on a QB sneak, then the 49ers went 99 yards for a touchdown. He added that the offense had only a couple of good drives.
McVay said travel, the Australia trip and the decision to play no preseason games did not affect the result. He said the team was ready and simply did not play well enough.
McVay said the Rams were not efficient in the kicking game and the 49ers had a big return. He also said the defense had chances but could not get off the field.
McVay said the loss starts with him and he will review the film to put players in better positions. He said the team would get back to work, with the next game next Monday night.

title: Shanahan Talks Injuries, Purdy's Big Game in Historic Win Over Rams
headline: Win over the Rams in Melbourne came with injury worries: WR De'Zhaun Stribling (ankle) and TE Jake Tonges (knee) both left and didn't return. Purdy and Mike Evans starred, and the plan is a more balanced backfield.
summary: Shanahan opened with the game's injuries. Stribling (ankle) and Tonges (knee) did not return, while Trent Williams and Christian McCaffrey left with cramps and came back. Stribling's Achilles was checked and is intact, but the team doesn't know how bad the ankle is. Shanahan was more grim about a knee injury at the end, saying it 'wasn't good' and 'not an ACL, MCL, I believe,' but there are issues still to sort out. The question didn't name the player, though it most likely concerned Tonges. He raved about Brock Purdy's play, especially the 99-yard drive where Purdy made off-schedule plays and ran for first downs. He also praised Purdy's long touchdown to Mike Evans, helped by strong protection against the Rams' pass rush. Shanahan said he loves calling plays for Evans, who moved the chains on third downs and gave the offense a red-zone fade option. The coach said the goal was to balance the backfield more, with Kaelon Black, McCaffrey and Deebo Samuel all sharing the load. He was glad to have Kittle, Greenlaw and Deebo back healthy and highlighted Renardo Green's return from a hamstring injury with an interception. He also called Fred Warner everything to him after Warner passed Patrick Willis for the franchise tackle record. The rest covered the Melbourne experience, the crowd and the travel, and the team now heads home to prepare for Week 2.

injuries.detail: Left with an ankle injury and did not return. His Achilles was checked and is intact, but the severity of the ankle injury is unknown.

Left with a knee injury and did not return. A later answer on a knee injury said it 'wasn't good' and is not an ACL or MCL, but issues remain and the team doesn't yet know more. The question didn't name the player, so this is probably Tonges.
Left briefly with cramps and came back.
Left briefly with cramps, returned quickly and missed little.
Returned from a hamstring injury that kept him out until this week, played at a high level and finished the game healthy.
Back on the field after missing a playoff game last season. Shanahan said his impact was felt all game.

signals.claim: Purdy remains the engine of the offense and can deliver on off-schedule plays and quick-game answers against a strong pass rush.
signals.note: Shanahan raved about Purdy's performance, including his running and the long touchdown, so his fantasy outlook looks strong.

signals.claim: Evans will be a featured target on third downs and in the red zone, including on fades.
signals.note: He got the first two third-down targets, had a big second-and-long, and was the target on the long touchdown, so he looks like a key part of the offense.
signals.quote: I love calling plays for Mike.

signals.claim: Black will continue to share backfield carries with McCaffrey as the team tries to balance the run game.
signals.note: Shanahan said both backs ran well and the balance was a stated goal, so Black has some standalone value and cuts into McCaffrey's workload.
signals.quote: that was a goal for us coming into this, trying to balance it out more

signals.claim: McCaffrey's workload will be more balanced with Black and Deebo getting carries.
signals.note: He is healthy after cramps, but the stated plan to spread carries caps his usage a bit.

signals.claim: Deebo will keep getting some carries as part of the balanced offense.
signals.note: Shanahan mentioned using him in the run game and he returned healthy, adding a touchdown on an off-schedule play from Purdy.
signals.quote: whether it was getting Deebo some carries

signals.claim: Green has recovered from his hamstring injury and is a full-time contributor again.
signals.note: He is a defensive player, but Shanahan was excited about his step forward this year, which matters in IDP leagues.
signals.quote: to play at the level he did, I thought was huge.

signals.claim: Kittle is back from injury and is playing at full capacity.
signals.note: With Tonges hurt, Kittle's role as the top tight end looks even more valuable.
signals.quote: Their impact you could feel throughout the whole game

topics.detail: Shanahan praised the line for holding up against the Rams' pass rush, especially on the long touchdown to Evans where Purdy had time on a seven-step drop. He said they needed to get the ball out quickly most of the game.
Warner passed Patrick Willis for the most tackles in franchise history. Shanahan said he means everything to him.

Shanahan pointed to the opening kick return of the third quarter, the 99-yard touchdown drive, and a fourth-and-goal stop inside the one as turning points. He said the team missed some chances in the second quarter.

He enjoyed the experience and the crowd of 100,021. He said the early arrival helped, and that the team would rather play 17 home games and does not like travel. Next up is Week 2, with a few extra days to recover.
Aaron Donald not playing did not change the game plan. Shanahan said they treated both ends the same way.
